intro1.say: This is atoma. It turns business ideas into working software.

intro2.say: Describe the tool you need. Agents build it, check it, and show you every step.

projects.say: Each project has a GitHub repository. Start empty, or from an existing one. Each run then opens a pull request.

goal.say: Describe what you want, in plain words.

criteria.say: Then say what done means. Routes with a status are checked over HTTP. Other lines are judged by review.

locked.say: The list is locked before planning starts.

live1.say: The run is live. Every model call and tool call appears as it happens.

live2.say: A planner splits the goal, a supervisor checks each phase, and a worker uses the tools.

delivered.say: Two minutes later, it is delivered, with its time, calls, tokens and cost.

acceptance.say: The final check does not take the model's word. It reads what the host observed, on servers the run started.

checklist.say: Each criterion is covered, with the request that proves it.

models.say: Each step uses the cheapest model that can do it. Haiku routes and builds, Opus plans, Sonnet checks.

call.say: Open any call to see its agent, its model, and what it produced.

published.say: The result is committed to the repository, and the next run starts from it.

partial1.say: When a run runs out of budget, or fails the final check, its work is kept.

partial2.say: atoma says why, in plain words, and what to do next.

partial3.say: Continue, and the next run picks up where it stopped.

tiers.say: Choose the model for each tier. An API key, the host's subscription, or your own ChatGPT account.

rerun.say: Rerun a delivered run on other models, and compare cost, time and result.

mcp.say: Claude Code, or any M C P client, can drive all of this, with thirty-nine tools.
mcp.show: Claude Code, or any MCP client, can drive all of this, with 39 tools.

skills.say: What works becomes a reusable skill, credited each time it succeeds.

trust.say: And every agent earns trust from its record, and loses it on failure.

outro.say: atoma is open source and self-hostable. Try it at atoma dot run.
outro.show: atoma is open source and self-hostable. Try it at atoma.run.
